title: Balance storage trace event state
description: Shape of the `state` field for balance-in-place-vs-ledger trace events.

storage.description: Whether the balance is one mutable number or a fold over immutable entries.

cachedBalance.description: Ledger only: a denormalized balance column is kept beside the entries.

balance.description: What a GET /balance would answer right now.

stored.description: The number physically kept in a column; absent for a pure ledger.

computed.description: The balance derived from the entries (from the snapshot, if any); ledger only.

drift.description: stored - computed. Non-zero means the two copies of the truth disagree.

entries.description: The append-only operation records, in order. Always empty for in-place storage.

amount.description: Signed: positive credits the account, negative debits it.

kind.description: A normal posting, the reversal of a wrong one, or its replacement.

running.description: Balance after this entry, folded from the start of the kept history.

snapshot.description: The cached fold, when one has been taken.

read.description: What the last balance read cost and where it came from.

rows.description: Rows the last read had to touch.

source.description: Which storage the last read used; 'none' before the first read.

inFlight.description: Operations being processed side by side; empty while they are serialized.

action.description: The signed amount this transaction wants to apply.

sawBalance.description: The balance this transaction read before deciding.

phase.description: Where this transaction got to; 'discarded' means its write was overwritten.

corrections.description: Wrong postings repaired by appending a reversal plus the right entry.

lostUpdates.description: Operations destroyed by a concurrent read-modify-write of the balance.

rewrites.description: Balances silently retyped, leaving no evidence that anything was wrong.

mutations.description: Entries deleted from an append-only book — holes in the audit trail.

violations.description: Business invariants (e.g. a floor) broken by concurrent appends.
